content.text: Investigation complete. All responsive provisions (§§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3) favour us.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 satisfies the preferred position. § 24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets (notice is a Customer-friendly formality only). § 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. § 24.3 applies a mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent standard to other assignments, and § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on Customer's change of control. § 13.3 adds a Customer-only licence transfer right tied to permitted assignments. The only wording short of preferred is that the competitor bar in § 24.2 is framed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute — a minor sub-element within our own control, noted rather than redlined. No provision binds Customer asymmetrically or gives Vendor a change-of-control exit, so there is nothing to flag.
